name: Kappa Ceti
description: A naked-eye star 9.1 parsecs away, 92% of the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 20630: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.936 +/- 0.025 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 0.919 +/- 0.025

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 20630: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.037 +/- 0.042

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 20630: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5776 +/- 81

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 20630: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 109.39 +/- 0.27 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 9 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 92% of the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 0.936 milliarcseconds, which gives 0.919 solar radii and 5,776 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 20630: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
